title: Why Is the Vulcan Salute So HARD? 🖖
description:
Try the Vulcan salute: split your fingers two and two, index and middle together, ring and pinky together. Can't? Your middle and ring fingers are the clingiest pair in your hand. On the back of your hand their cords (the tendons that straighten your fingers) are tied together by little straps, and your brain tends to move the two as a team. When scientists asked people to move one finger at a time, the ring finger was the worst at moving alone and the middle finger came next (Häger-Ross & Schieber, J Neurosci 2000). The salute asks you to split exactly those two. Even Star Trek actors reportedly set their fingers with the other hand, off camera; Leonard Nimoy took the gesture from a Jewish priestly blessing he saw as a boy. Can you split your fingers?
